defect.title: Reopen from Dock or open -a does not restore the Status window
defect.note: applicationShouldHandleReopen calls makeKeyAndOrderFront when hasVisibleWindows is false. After AX close: glass_probe axWindowCount=0, extras still present. proctor_apps activate: activated true, windows [], 8000ms, note says menu-bar-only. open -a /Applications/Proctor.app: still axWindows=0. System Events click Window/Proctor restored 640x592 at 946,99. Likely cause: after walkthroughCompleted=1 the app is .accessory and NSApp.windows.first is not ordered front by activate/open -a; the Window menu item is. Fixed: WindowPresentation.shouldPresentMain asks whether a window titled Proctor is on screen instead of trusting hasVisibleWindows; reopen orders it front or posts for the scene to be created. Verified on .build/Proctor.app: cg 0 / ax 0 before, cg 1 820x1009 / ax 1 after open -a. Six tests in WindowPresentationTests cover the rule. Verified on the installed artifact after reinstall: cg 0 / ax 0 before, cg 1 640x592 / ax 1 titled Proctor after open -a.

defect.title: Status window kept claiming Ready while the agent was wedged
defect.note: First filed against a killed agent and retracted: a kill fails connect() at once and the window recovers within one 2s tick (Agent down at t+0.71s). Sweep L half-open found the real shape. With the agent held by SIGSTOP the socket is accepted and never answered, the poll blocks in read(), isChecking latches, and the window showed Ready with green grants past 25 seconds while a driven proctor_doctor never returned. Fixed by an opt-in SocketClient.ioTimeoutSeconds, default 0 so the shim is unchanged, with AgentModel polling at 5s. Verified: Agent down at t+7.12s, recovered after SIGCONT.

defect.title: Installed Proctor.app is Developer ID signed but not notarised or stapled
defect.note: spctl -a -vv /Applications/Proctor.app → rejected, source=Unnotarized Developer ID, origin=Developer ID Application: Luke Rhodes (H4HGFL52W7). stapler validate → does not have a ticket stapled. codesign reports runtime hardened, timestamp 18 Aug 2026. This is the artifact the macos-glass lane attached (commit 1c6500c51b24). CASE-0024 fails on it. Fixed by scripts/install.sh on 2026-08-19: notarised through the proctor keychain profile and stapled. spctl now returns accepted, source=Notarized Developer ID; stapler validate passes.

defect.title: Campaign recorded a refusal the product does not perform (profile filtering)
defect.note: CASE-0002 was armed with "swapped profile filter from full to core; verified proctor_guest refused". Measured: a core-profile shim executes proctor_guest and proctor_policy when they are named. That is the documented contract (MCPServer.swift:123) rather than a product defect, so the campaign record was corrected and the arming rewritten around what the profile does change, the advertised catalogue: 21 names on full, 10 on core.

defect.title: The drawn pointer was not excluded from screen capture
defect.note: Found while arming CASE-0008: with the exclusion at its default the run panel and the takeover tint reported sharingState 0 and refused every capture, while the drawn pointer reported 1 and photographed cleanly at 3456x2234. It covers every display, so Proctor's own pointer entered any display-scoped capture taken during a run, against the principle the other two panels are built on. Cause: it is the only one of the three that changes window level at runtime, and sharingType does not survive the change. Fixed by setting level and sharing together in one place. The obvious suspect, that the window server refuses .none at screenSaver level, was measured and ruled out first.
